hypotheses.statement: Management view (CRO): growth slowed because a new competitor is undercutting us on price and taking new deals
hypotheses.implication: New-business losses to price do not explain the slowdown: win rate held at 23-24% and new ARR rose; only 17% of churned customers left for a competitor and 14% cite price. A price response or more sales capacity does not address the cause.

hypotheses.statement: Growth slowed because churn rose, concentrated in first-year customers after the February 2025 onboarding cut
hypotheses.implication: Retention, especially onboarding of new customers, is the first lever; the causal link to the onboarding cut rests on timing and exit interviews, not a controlled test.

hypotheses.statement: Growth slowed because sales capacity or pipeline was insufficient
hypotheses.implication: Adding account executives treats a constraint the data does not show; pipeline grew and deals won rose while new ARR was flat.

hypotheses.statement: Expansion ARR fell for the same reason as churn: customers who never fully implement the product do not expand
hypotheses.implication: If true, fixing onboarding also recovers part of the 1.3 EUR M expansion decline; no account-level expansion data is available to test it.

hypotheses.statement: Hiring 30 account executives in Q1 2026 will add 9 EUR M of new ARR in 2026, as the CRO states
hypotheses.implication: 9 EUR M is the full-productivity run-rate of 30 AEs at 300 EUR k each; with a 9-month ramp the 2026 contribution is lower and depends on ramp shape and pipeline.
